title: Stock Market Update: Futures Slightly Higher Following Yesterday's Fed Decision

organizations.name: fed decision  futures slightly higher following yesterday's fed

text:
Futures Slightly Higher Following Yesterday's Fed Decision 27-Sep-18 08:01 ET Market is Closed [BRIEFING.COM] S&P futures vs fair value: +1.80. Nasdaq futures vs fair value: +22.00.
Following Wednesday's sharp drop in the final minutes, the S&P 500 futures are trading slightly higher this morning, up 0.1%, as investors continue to digest yesterday's policy statement from the Federal Reserve, which included a rate hike of 25 basis points. For the week, the S&P 500 enters today's session down 0.8%.
The focus yesterday was on the Fed's removal of the word 'accommodative' from its policy statement, which led some to believe that the central bank could be moving towards slowing monetary tightening. However, Fed Chairman Jerome Powell followed up by saying the language change didn't signal a change in the Fed's path for rate hikes.
Although not directly related to the markets, many investors will likely be tuning in to the Brett Kavanaugh hearing on Capitol Hill today, so volume might be lighter-than-usual. Christine Ford has accused Judge Kavanaugh, who is President Trump's Supreme Court nominee, of sexually assaulting her back in high school, which Mr. Kavanaugh has denied. The two will be telling their sides of the story before the Senate Judiciary Committee starting at 10:00 AM ET.
Investors will receive a big batch of economic data at 8:30 AM ET this morning, including the advanced readings for August International Trade in Goods (Briefing.com consensus -$71.0 billion), Retail Inventories, and Wholesale Inventories, Durable Goods Orders for August (Briefing.com consensus +1.8%), the third estimate for Q2 GDP (Briefing.com consensus 4.3%), and weekly Initial Claims (Briefing.com consensus 209K). In addition, August Pending Home Sales (Briefing.com consensus -0.4%) will be released at 10:00 AM ET.
Looking at other markets, U.S. Treasuries are extending yesterday's rally, pushing yields lower across the curve, with the benchmark 10-yr yield down one basis point at 3.05%. The U.S. Dollar Index is up 0.3% at 94.19, and WTI crude futures are higher by 1.0% at $72.27/bbl.
In U.S. corporate news: Apple (AAPL 223.40, +2.98): +1.4% after being initiated with an 'Overweight' rating at JPMorgan Chase, which also raised its target price for Apple to $272/share. Bed Bath & Beyond (BBBY 16.17, -2.64): -14.0% after missing earnings and revenue estimates and reporting a decline in same-store sales. The company also lowered its guidance for FY19. Advanced Micro (AMD 31.73, -0.46): -1.4% after being downgraded to 'Market Perform' from 'Outperform' at Northland Capital.
Reviewing overnight developments: Japan's Nikkei -0.8%, Hong Kong's Hang Seng -0.4%, China's Shanghai Composite -0.5%, India's Sensex -0.6%. In news: Major European indices trade in mixed fashion with Italy's MIB (-1.3%) showing relative weakness. UK's FTSE +0.2%, France's CAC -0.1%, Germany's DAX -0.2%.
